title: React, JavaScript & TypeScript Interview Questions & Answers

questions.question: What is React and why is it efficient?
questions.answer: React is a JavaScript library for building UI through reusable components.
reasons_efficient: Virtual DOM - batches and minimizes real DOM updates via diffing
Declarative model - describe the UI for a given state, React handles DOM mutations
Component-based architecture - reuse and isolate logic
Fiber architecture - prioritize and interrupt rendering work so UI stays responsive

questions.question: How does React work internally?
questions.answer: When state changes, React calls the render function to produce a new React element tree (Virtual DOM). It runs reconciliation - diffing the new tree against the previous one using Fiber, which breaks work into units that can be paused, prioritized, and resumed. React computes the minimal set of DOM mutations needed and applies them in a commit phase.
key_points: Render phase: builds new virtual DOM tree
Reconciliation: diffs old vs new tree
Fiber: interruptible, prioritized units of work
Commit phase: applies minimal DOM mutations
Hooks (useState/useEffect) are tracked per fiber node as a linked list - must be called in same order every render

questions.question: What is the most challenging task you handled in your project?
questions.answer: Personal/experience-based question - no universal answer. Use STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result).
good_examples: A production bug with unclear root cause
questions.tip: Show your thought process, the tradeoffs you considered, and a measurable outcome (e.g., 'reduced load time by 40%' or 'eliminated a recurring crash').

questions.question: Is JavaScript tightly coupled or loosely coupled?
questions.answer: JavaScript itself is dynamically-typed and encourages loose coupling through first-class functions, closures, ES modules, and prototypal inheritance. However, how tightly or loosely coupled your code is depends on how you write it.
key_points: Global variables and direct DOM manipulation create tight coupling
Modules, dependency injection, and pub/sub patterns create loose coupling
The language provides tools for loose coupling but doesn't enforce it

questions.question: Why do we use TypeScript?
questions.answer: TypeScript adds static typing on top of JavaScript, catching type errors at compile time instead of runtime.
benefits: Better IDE autocomplete and refactoring support
Self-documenting code - types act as inline docs
Fewer runtime bugs (e.g., 'undefined is not a function')
Compiles to plain JS - no runtime cost

questions.question: How does 'extends' work in TypeScript and what is the difference between type and interface?
questions.answer: extends lets an interface or type inherit members from another. Interfaces use 'extends', types use intersections (&).
differences: Declaration merging: interfaces can be declared multiple times and merge; types cannot
Extending: interfaces use 'extends'; types use intersections (&)
Union/primitives: type can represent unions, primitives, tuples (type ID = string | number); interfaces cannot
Object shapes: largely interchangeable for plain object shapes
questions.guideline: Use interface for public API shapes/objects that might be extended. Use type for unions, tuples, and complex compositions.

questions.question: How does Redux work, from installation to usage in a project?
questions.answer: A single immutable store holds app state. Components dispatch actions (plain objects describing what happened). Reducers (pure functions) take current state + action and return new state. Store notifies subscribed components, which re-render with new state.
key_principles: State is read-only - only changed via dispatched actions
Changes are made by pure reducer functions

questions.question: Have you used Redux Toolkit (RTK) or TanStack Query?
questions.answer: Experience-based question. RTK is the modern recommended way to write Redux with less boilerplate. TanStack Query solves server-state (data fetching/caching) rather than client/UI state.

redux_toolkit.description: Reduces boilerplate significantly. Includes Immer (write 'mutating' code that's actually immutable under the hood), built-in DevTools setup, and createAsyncThunk for async logic.

tanstack_query.description: Handles caching, background refetching, stale-while-revalidate, and deduplication automatically for server data.

questions.tip: Many teams use RTK for client state + TanStack Query for server state, reducing boilerplate around loading/error states.

questions.question: What is the difference between bind and apply in JavaScript?
questions.answer: Both set the 'this' context for a function. apply calls the function immediately with args as an array. bind returns a new function with 'this' permanently bound, without calling it immediately.
questions.related: call(thisArg, ...args) - like apply but args passed individually, also calls immediately
questions.tip: Mnemonic: Apply takes an Array. Bind is for later.

questions.question: What has been your experience with useCallback and useMemo in real projects?
questions.answer: useMemo memoizes a computed value, recomputing only when dependencies change - useful for expensive calculations. useCallback memoizes a function reference - useful when passing callbacks to memoized child components (React.memo) to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
questions.tip: Don't overuse them - they have their own overhead. Profile first with React DevTools, then memoize only parts causing actual performance issues (expensive computations or components re-rendering due to unstable prop references).

questions.question: What is the role of the dependency array in useEffect?
questions.answer: The dependency array tells React when to re-run the effect - it re-runs only when one of the listed values changes (via Object.is comparison) between renders.

behaviors.empty_array: Effect runs once, after initial mount only
behaviors.with_deps: Effect runs on mount and whenever any listed dependency changes

common_pitfalls: Omitting a dependency that's actually used inside the effect - causes stale closures/bugs (ESLint exhaustive-deps rule catches this)
Including objects/functions recreated every render - causes infinite loops unless wrapped in useMemo/useCallback
